title: St Albans Cathedral, St Albans, England, United Kingdom - Inside the Cathedral
author: Tiago CarvE
notes: Room tone inside St Albans Cathedral (England), 48 kHz FLAC. Very quiet, even, reverberant air (-43 LUFS, LRA ~4 dB): low rumble plus a soft, far-off wash of visitors in the nave; nothing close, no organ or music. Starts after a faint knock at ~101 s. Two very faint distant voice blips near 174 s and 190 s sit ~15 dB under the bed. Needs a lot of gain; hp ~40 Hz trims the sub-rumble.

Dense, diffuse hubbub (energy 250 Hz-2 kHz) with steady china and cutlery clinks; no single voice stands out on the spectrogram and LRA is 4.9 dB. title: Schopenhauerstraße 8, 14467 Potsdam, Deutschland - Dishes in Kitchen

notes: Dishes being sorted in the kitchen of a Baptist church in Potsdam after the service (Zoom H6, 48k FLAC). Event: a run of 6 light ceramic clinks: plates and cups being stacked (tonal ring at ~2.4 kHz and ~750 Hz). Floor about -57 dBFS; the event is 27-46 dB over it. No voices. Close perspective, as at the table.

title: Life goes by as St Mary's Church clock strikes 12 noon, Halesworth IP19 8LL, UK
author: Peter Cusack
notes: The 12th (last) stroke of St Mary's Church clock striking noon, recorded beside the churchyard in Halesworth, Suffolk (320k MP3). The bell rings with a hum at ~370 Hz and ~170 Hz and decays about 30 dB in-band before the clip ends. Jackdaws call faintly at 6-8 kHz in the tail. title: Big Ben 11am
author: London Sound Survey
notes: Big Ben, London: the 11th (final) hour stroke at 11 am (London Sound Survey, 2009). Hum with partials at ~320 Hz and ~500 Hz, decaying ~28 dB until the file's own fade at 73.5 s. Caveat: central-London traffic rumble below ~200 Hz, which hp ~250 Hz mostly removes. Lossy OGG with a slight spectral notch near 5.5 kHz. Earlier strokes come every ~4 s and overlap.

title: Bourdon Bell From Inside The Cathedral - Worcester Cathedral.UK
author: david.j.pitt
notes: Worcester Cathedral's bourdon striking noon, heard from INSIDE the nave (MixPre + MKH 8020, 320k MP3). Final stroke: a deep ~240 Hz hum with the cathedral's long reverb, ringing on for ~5 s before sinking into the interior air. This is how the tower bell would sound from inside the great hall. Caveat: high broadband interior noise floor (heating or air, 20-800 Hz); the hum is only ~10 dB over it a

title: 11 Rue Saint-Etienne, 45000 Orléans, France - Death Knell
author: colinedevalence
notes: Death knell tolled in Orleans, France on 21 April 2025 (FLAC, mono). A single stroke of a medium church bell (partials ~500/760/1100/1400 Hz), from a slow 5.02-s toll, so each stroke stands alone. The in-band level falls ~18-20 dB before the next stroke, but the ~760 Hz hum is still faintly ringing at the cut, so it needs a ~0.8 s fade-out. Rock-steady level (10-s medians all within 1 dB). Recorded fairly close (-14 LUFS), not far off, so to place it 'some way off' play it quieter with a gentle low-pass (~4-5 kHz). title: XC647448 Tawny Owl
author: David Tattersley
notes: Strix aluco, male territorial song, near Rosemarkie, Highland, SCOTLAND (2021-05-10, 320k MP3). One complete song: 'hoooo' (2.3-3.0 s), pause, then 'hu... hu-hu-hu-hooo' quaver (7.1-8.9 s), ~800 Hz, about 38 dB over the in-band floor. Low wind or sea rumble below 300 Hz, cut by hp 400.

title: XC785197 Tawny Owl
author: B Whyte
notes: Strix aluco, male hooting song, Culloden Woods, Highland, SCOTLAND (2023-03-10). Clip has one song: hoot at 0.5-1.6 s, then the quavering second part at 4.2-5.3 s (~850 Hz, with harmonics). It stops before 11 s, where the background noise jumps. LF noise is cut by hp 400.

title: XC611876 Tawny Owl
author: Scott Wotherspoon
notes: Strix aluco, male song, near Falkirk, SCOTLAND (2020-12-31, 192k MP3). One full song: 'hoooo' at 81.7-82.7 s, a faint second note, 'hu' at 87.0 s, then a quavering 'hu-hu-hooo' at 87.7-89.2 s (~880 Hz plus harmonics to 3.5 kHz). A second owl is very faint at ~84-85 s. Distant traffic rumble below 300 Hz, cut by hp 400.

title: XC459193 Tawny Owl
author: Peter Stronach
notes: Strix aluco, female contact call 'ke-wick', Inverness (Inbhir Nis), Highland, SCOTLAND (2019-02-25). A single clean call (fundamental sweep ~1.0-1.8 kHz, strong harmonics). Very low background, probably filtered by the recordist; quiet file (peak -27 dBFS), so normalise.

title: XC1184870 Tawny Owl
author: Mark James Pearson
notes: Strix aluco, a single female-type 'ke-wick' call, Wigginton, York, England, UK (2026-09-27). Isolated: the previous call ends at 14.6 s. Caveat: 24 kHz, 64 kbps mono MP3 (top ~12 kHz), but the call's energy is at 1-4 kHz. A second Scottish-equivalent ke-wick could not be found that was this clean.
